decisionRule.interpretation: Development validation only. Expected outcomes and pair labels never enter cognition. No quota applies in production. Any valid disappointing result is retained without quality resampling.

cases.rememberedContent: I remember waiting after rehearsal for Mara after she said she would drive me home; everyone else left, my calls went unanswered, and I eventually took the bus alone.

priorMeaning.summary: With Mara, plans sometimes collapse at the last minute and the explanation comes later, so I have learned to expect both the disruption and the silence before I know why.
parts: The delayed explanation is already part of what makes plans with her feel unreliable in the moment.

trigger.observableAction: Years later, Mara canceled a weekend hike shortly before we were due to leave and explained the next morning that an emergency shift had come up at work.

trigger.observableAction: Years later, while reviewing an old family phone account, Mara showed that several messages from those missed plans had been sent to a number that stopped forwarding to me, including one from the rehearsal night saying her car had broken down.

cases.rememberedContent: I remember my aunt taking a medical form addressed to me, saying she would explain it when things were calmer, and putting it in a drawer while I kept wondering what it meant.

priorMeaning.summary: My aunt often delays difficult explanations while trying to shield me, and I experience that delay as both care and exclusion from information that concerns me.
parts: Even when she later explains, the period of being kept outside the information is part of the meaning for me.

trigger.observableAction: Years later, my aunt set aside a complicated insurance notice, said she would explain it after her shift, and went through it with me that evening.

trigger.observableAction: Years later, she showed me the old clinic file and a written instruction from the hospital telling guardians not to discuss the preliminary diagnosis until a confirmatory test was complete, then explained why she had put the form away.

cases.rememberedContent: I remember presenting a sketch in art class, hearing two people laugh behind me, and rushing through the rest because I assumed they were laughing at my work.

priorMeaning.summary: When I hear ambiguous laughter while presenting, I can treat it as ridicule before I know its cause and withdraw; I already recognize this as a recurring reaction of mine.
parts: The uncertainty about what the laughter means is part of the pattern, not evidence that it was actually about me.

trigger.observableAction: Years later, during a design critique, I heard laughter from the back of the room without knowing why, shortened my presentation, and avoided questions afterward.

trigger.observableAction: Years later, a class recording surfaced showing that the laughter began when a paint jar tipped over behind me and that the students were looking at the spill rather than at my sketch.

cases.rememberedContent: I remember a coach writing 'we need to talk' on my training sheet, saying there was not enough time after practice, and leaving me unsure whether I had done something wrong.

priorMeaning.summary: Brief evaluative signals followed by delayed explanation leave me suspended between concern and hope; I already expect that uncertainty whenever feedback is postponed.
parts: Until the explanation arrives, I tend to experience the waiting itself as part of being evaluated.

trigger.observableAction: Years later, a manager wrote 'let's discuss' on a draft, had to leave for another meeting, and gave the full feedback at our scheduled one-on-one the following morning.
